checks.comparison: SmoothObjective f L := (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧ ∀ x y, ‖gradient f x − gradient f y‖ ≤ L‖x − y‖ on Point d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). This is Assumption 1.1 (differentiable and L-smooth). It is required in admissible with I.f and p.L, and valid contains 0 < p.L.
Requiring HasGradientAt everywhere is the meaning of "differentiable" with the gradient in an inner product space. Nothing else is added.
LowerBounded I.f I.lower := ∀ x, I.lower ≤ I.f x, with lower the hidden Instance field (Rennala.Instance d = (f, lower)). This is Assumption 1.2 with f^* = I.lower.
The extra admissible clause I.f p.x0 − I.lower ≤ p.Δ is the reviewed adaptation (Δ is a supplied upper bound on the source gap), not a source assumption change.

admissible requires IsStochasticGradient (Point p.d) Ω μ I.f g p.σ, whose elaborated record has these fields: measurable (uncurry g), integrable (g x), unbiased (∫ g x ω ∂μ = gradient f x). The oracle is O = gradientOracle P g, and every tape coordinate has law μ (∀ c, P.map (η ↦ η c) = μ). This is unbiasedness of ∇f(x;ξ), ξ ∼ D_ξ, for all x.

Measurability and integrability are the accepted implicit conditions. The existential choice of Ω (in Type), μ, P and g describes the hidden oracle construction. It is not visible to the algorithm and adds no assumption on f.
The IsStochasticGradient fields variance_integrable and variance (∫‖g x ω − gradient f x‖² ∂μ ≤ σ²), together with 0 ≤ p.σ in valid, give Assumption 1.3.
Nothing beyond integrability of the variance integrand, which the source integral presupposes.

SampleIndependent T m γ x0 g P := ∀ k, IndepFun (η ↦ η(auxSample m k)) (η ↦ (i : Fin k) ↦ (vertex(m(i+1)), vertex(auxNode m (i+1)), η(auxSample m i))) P. This is ξ^k independent of {(x^{i+1}, z^{i+1}, ξ^i)}_{i<k} for all k (Condition 1), with x, z and ξ the realised main branch, auxiliary points and samples. admissible requires it at γ = stepSize p.L p.σ p.ε p.R, which equals publicInput.gamma, the step birch actually runs.

There is no IID or product requirement beyond Condition 1 and the marginals, so the source dependence model is preserved. The measurable spaces are the standard pi/product spaces with the WithLp (Borel) structure on Point d.
ReprContained T m := ∀ k, T.repr(auxNode m k) ≤ T.repr(m k), i.e. multiset containment repr(z^k) ⊆ repr(x^k) (Condition 2). It is in valid, as a property of the public method.
Multiset ≤ is the accepted reading. Placing it in valid is correct because, with a fixed tree, it depends only on tree and branch.
DistanceBounded T m R := ∀ k, (dist(m k, auxNode m k) : ℝ) ≤ R (Condition 3). It is in valid with 0 ≤ p.R.
Finite real R is the accepted interpretation. The condition is structural, so valid is the right place.

valid: 0 < L, 0 ≤ σ, 0 < ε, 0 ≤ Δ, 0 ≤ R, together with tree.WellFormed, IsMainBranch branch, ReprContained and DistanceBounded. These are the accepted domains. WellFormed is present, which resolves my earlier alg-unit note about defaults for ill-formed trees.

publicInput: d, gamma := stepSize p.L p.σ p.ε p.R, x0, tree, branch, K := horizon p.L p.σ p.ε p.Δ p.R. admissible uses the same stepSize arguments in SampleIndependent, and the same p.tree, p.branch and p.x0. So Condition 1 constrains exactly the run that is executed.

Hypotheses on the method are in valid, and hypotheses on f and the oracle are in admissible. successful states only the visible accuracy criterion. There is no implication or work premise inside successful, and no conclusion is assumed.
All seven assumption clauses appear exactly once (A1, A2, A3, C1 in admissible; C2, C3 in valid). The only extra premise is the gap bound f(x0) − lower ≤ Δ from the reviewed plan adaptation.

successful is Measurable output ∧ Integrable ‖gradient I.f (output ω)‖² ∧ ∫‖gradient I.f (output ω)‖² ∂P ≤ p.ε, matching the plan design criterion character for character. Tuning uses the reviewed Algorithms.stepSize and horizon.

allowedAlgorithm q A := A = birch q pins the factory to the reviewed Algorithm 1 implementation. Query, Reply and Output are all Point p.d. numOracles is the default 1, matching birch and gradientOracle.

The oracle tape law P is arbitrary subject to marginals μ and Condition 1. Expectations in successful are explicit integrals against the supplied ProbabilityMeasure. The template product of birch's uniform seed law with P gives the independent output index.
The setup owns the assumption nodes and the spec, and no convergence claim. The rate is in Proofs (main_theorem) and the public wrapper.
Conditions 2 and 3 use the reviewed Tree.repr (multiset) and Tree.dist (ℕ, cast to ℝ).

Reused providers, inspected through their records: IsStochasticGradient (E Ω, instances, μ, f, g, σ), whose fields match Assumption 1.3 as checked in the plan review; Rennala.Instance d = (f : Point d → ℝ, lower : ℝ); IndepFun; HasGradientAt/gradient; and alg-unit declarations already accepted. I verified all 325 referenced records' SHA-256 (0 mismatches). Unit axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

The setup composes the accepted alg unit (Public, birch, stepSize, horizon, gradientOracle, Tree API) into a Setup whose Params, Public and publicInput match the plan design ledger (9 Params fields d, L, σ, ε, Δ, R, x0, tree, branch). spec is in namespace outputs.Setups.BirchSgd, equal to its module path.

Δ = 0, R = 0 and σ = 0 are allowed by valid and handled by stepSize/horizon. K may be 0 (output space Fin 1). Positivity of L and ε avoids division by zero. The existential Ω is restricted to Type 0, a harmless universe convention for a Prop-level description of the sample space.

There is a single consumer T in identical mode. The compiled spec contains exactly the shared hypotheses (A1, A2, A3, C1 in admissible; C2, C3 in valid) and the parameters of T's context. f, f^* and g are hidden in Instance and the oracle; R, tree, branch, x0, L, σ, ε and Δ are Params fields; K and γ are derived. Nothing is strengthened beyond the reviewed Δ upper bound.
